title: Structures and magnetic properties of rhombus-shaped tetranuclear [Ln4] clusters: Dy4 cluster displaying single molecule magnet behavior

synthesis.procedure: Clusters 1–3 were prepared by the same recipe. Ln(dbm)3·2H2O (Ln = Tb for 1; 0.03 mmol; 0.02612 g given based on the Dy salt) was added to a solution of Schiff-base ligand HL (0.03 mmol, 0.00762 g) in 20 mL CH2Cl2/CH3CN (v/v = 1:3). The mixture was stirred for about 30 min at room temperature, transferred to a 30 mL glass reaction vial, and heated at 75 °C for 10 h. After natural cooling to room temperature, yellow block crystals of 1 suitable for single-crystal X-ray diffraction were obtained.

reagents.name: Tb(dbm)3·2H2O
reagents.amount: 0.03 mmol (0.02612 g reported based on Dy salt)

synthesis.temperature: stirred at room temperature, then heated at 75 °C
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solvothermal reaction in 30 mL glass vial
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: naturally cooled to room temperature; yellow block crystals obtained

properties.summary: Dc susceptibility under 1.0 kOe (300–2.0 K) gives room-temperature χMT = 47.23 cm3 K mol−1 (expected 47.28 for four free TbIII). χMT remains nearly constant 300–70 K, then decreases to 38.56 cm3 K mol−1 at 2.0 K, attributed to weak antiferromagnetic exchange and/or thermal depopulation of Stark sublevels. Zero-dc-field ac susceptibility (3.0 Oe oscillating field) shows no evident temperature-dependent χ″ signals, so no SMM behavior.

measurements.conditions: zero dc field, ac oscillating field 3.0 Oe

synthesis.procedure: Clusters 1–3 were prepared by the same recipe. Ln(dbm)3·2H2O (Ln = Dy for 2; 0.03 mmol, 0.02612 g) was added to a solution of HL (0.03 mmol, 0.00762 g) in 20 mL CH2Cl2/CH3CN (v/v = 1:3). After stirring ~30 min at room temperature, the solution was transferred to a 30 mL glass reaction vial and heated at 75 °C for 10 h. Natural cooling to room temperature afforded yellow block crystals of 2.
synthesis.temperature: stirred at room temperature, then heated at 75 °C
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solvothermal reaction in 30 mL glass vial
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: naturally cooled to room temperature; yellow block crystals obtained

properties.summary: Room-temperature χMT = 56.86 cm3 K mol−1 under 1.0 kOe (expected 56.68 for four free DyIII), decreasing to 35.75 cm3 K mol−1 at 2.0 K, consistent with weak antiferromagnetic exchange and/or Stark-level depopulation. Temperature-dependent χ″ appears below 20 K with χ″ shoulder peaks and a rapid rise below 9.0 K, indicating slow magnetic relaxation with QTM and more than one relaxation process. Frequency-dependent ac data under zero dc field and Arrhenius fitting of ln(τ) vs T−1 (2.0–16.0 K) give ΔE/kB = 103.7 K and τ0 = 8.41 × 10−9 s, evidencing SMM behavior. Cole–Cole fits to the generalized Debye model give α = 0.13–0.62, indicating a wide distribution of relaxation times and possible two-process behavior that could not be fully fitted.
